newsitem.title: USA: Westinghouse posts $34 million fourth-quarter loss.
newsitem.headline: Westinghouse posts $34 million fourth-quarter loss.

text.p: Westinghouse Electric Corp., completing its transformation into a broadcasting powerhouse, said Tuesday it lost $34 million in its fourth quarter as restructuring costs continued to take a bite out of earnings.
However, the company's radio operations posted an exceptionally strong performance and its industrial group, which has been sluggish, posted higher profits.
Total fourth-quarter sales grew to $2.5 billion from $1.9 billion a year ago.

The results for the most recent quarter included a one-time charge of $91 million related to the company's restructuring, while the year-earlier period included a charge of $125 million for restructuring and litigation.
The most recent loss, equal to 8 cents a share, compared with a loss of $7 million, or 2 cents a share, a year earlier.

Over the past 16 months, Westinghouse has acquired CBS, Infinity Broadcasting and two country-themed cable television networks as it transforms itself into a broadcasting company. At the same time, Westinghouse has announced the spinoff of its industrial group, scheduled to occur this summer.

For the year, Westinghouse earned $30 million, or 7 cents a share, on revenues of $8.45 billion. In 1995, the company earned $15 million on revenues of $5.60 billion. Its per share result for 1995 was a loss of 5 cents due to dividends paid on preferred shares.

In the fourth quarter, radio operations posted a 37 percent increase in earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization, while sales rose 10 percent. Those operations also posted improved performance for the full year.

"We're encouraged by the strong growth in radio, which should accelerate as we leverage the new opportunities in the combined Infinity and CBS radio groups," Chairman Michael Jordan said in a statement.

Westinghouse's industrial group -- Thermo King, energy systems, power generation and government operations -- posted an 18 percent rise in profits for the fourth quarter excluding special charges on sales that rose nearly 8 percent.
For the full year, sales were flat compared with 1995 and profits, excluding special items, were down 10 percent.

Westinghouse spokesman Kevin Ramundo said the group's higher quarterly results were due largely to Thermo King, a refrigerated transport unit, and power generation. Both units posted increased profits.

"Our industrial businesses steadily improved during 1996," Jordan said in the statement. "As we prepare for the spinoff (of them) we believe that this group is positioned to grow in all of its markets."
At the company's CBS network, earnings fell in the fourth quarter and the full year due to lower demographic ratings coupled with increased costs, Ramundo said.
Those results are on a pro forma basis. Westinghouse acquired CBS in November 1995.

Jordan said he was optimistic about future performance for the network. "As the only one of the top three networks to increase household ratings during the fall season, CBS is solidifying its move into second place in the ratings," he said. "In the November sweeps, CBS had the most affiliates ranked first in their markets."
Westinghouse's stock traded at $18.375, up $1, in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
